summary.text: 请 means “ask” or “request,” and can also mean “invite” or function as “please.” It is the standardized simplified form of 請, whose historical analysis combines speech-related 言 with 青 as a sound element.

formation.text: 請 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 言 contributes the speech-related meaning category, and 青 supplies the sound. The simplified graph 请 retains the same construction through 讠, the simplified component corresponding to 言.

components.text: 讠 is the simplified form of 言 and marks the speech-related category in 请. It is the conventional simplified component form in this graph, not a separate ancient replacement stage.
青 supplies the sound in 請. Its modern Mandarin reading qīng resembles 請 qǐng; Baxter–Sagart gives a historical comparison within the same system, supporting the sound relation.

sound.text: In modern Mandarin, 青 qīng corresponds to 請 qǐng. In Baxter–Sagart 2014, 青 is MC tsheng, OC *[s.r̥]ˤeŋ, and 請 qǐng is MC tshjengX, OC *[tsʰ]eŋʔ; the distinct historical forms support a sound relationship.

history.text: The traditional graph 請 is represented in the supplied curated image by a seal-style rendering. That image is a modern vector redraw, not an ancient artifact. A historical lexicographic analysis identifies 言 as semantic and 青 as phonetic, but the dossier establishes no dated sequence of earlier forms.

请 is standardized as the simplified counterpart of 請 through the simplified component series 讠 corresponding to 言. This documents a modern standardization relationship, not an ancient graphic chronology.

uncertainties.text: The historical gloss 謁也 does not establish the earliest attested use, and no dated earliest specimen or graphic sequence for 請 was verified in this dossier.

The dictionary records several readings and uses under 請, including qīng in 請室 and qíng uses glossed as 通情 and 通擎. Their relationship to qǐng and the chronology of the request, invitation, petition, inquiry, greeting, and respectful-request uses remain unresolved here.

senses.text: The character is used for asking, requesting, or entreating. The dossier gives these as current glosses but does not establish the earliest attestation of this sense.
Invite is a recorded use of 請, but the supplied evidence does not establish its chronological relation to asking or requesting.
A respectful-request use is recorded, including a cited classical example; the dossier does not date its emergence or establish a path from the other senses.
A historical lexicographic gloss is 謁也. It is a recorded gloss, not proof of the character’s earliest attested use or hypothetical original meaning.

limitations.text: The cited dictionary groups request, entreaty, engagement, invitation, petition, inquiry, greeting, welcoming a deity, and respectful-request uses, but the evidence does not establish their order or semantic connections.
The separate qīng and qíng readings and uses are recorded, but the dossier does not show whether or how they connect historically to qǐng.

overview.text: 请 means “ask” or “request,” and also “invite” or “please.” It is the simplified form of 請: speech-related 言 appears as 讠, while 青 supplies a sound cue.

components.text: 讠 is the simplified speech component, corresponding to 言 in 請.
青 is the sound element; its modern Mandarin qīng resembles 请’s qǐng, and historical reconstructions support the relationship.

relationships.text: 请 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 請, formed through the simplified component series 讠 corresponding to 言.
讠 is the simplified speech-related semantic component in 请, corresponding to 言 in 請.

青 is the stated sound component in 請. Modern Mandarin 青 qīng and 請 qǐng are compared; Baxter–Sagart 2014 gives 青 MC tsheng, OC *[s.r̥]ˤeŋ and 請 qǐng MC tshjengX, OC *[tsʰ]eŋʔ, supporting a historical sound relationship.
